patent_grounding.rationale: The added VANE–LEVER coupling is directly supported: claim 1 places each lever at the corresponding vane pivot axis and states it turns the vane, while the description says vane axes are secured via the guide-vane lever and vanes are adjusted via their axes by turning the ring. The linkage, threshold rupture, first-arm survival, and post-fracture holding/load relief are also supported by cited passages. No unsupported actuator/controller is asserted.

functional_completeness.rationale: The model captures the patent-supported vane, lever, link, common adjusting element, selective overload rupture, load relief, and post-break holding path. Optional ring and bolt construction are appropriately qualified as a disclosed configuration/illustrative embodiment rather than mandatory universal features.

flow_consistency.rationale: The VANE–LEVER interface uses mechanical_rotational ports and a distinct rotational flow; the link-to-lever and link-to-adjuster couplings use mechanical_linear flows. No incompatible transformation is represented by a direct connection.

claim_traceability.rationale: The central assembly and threshold rupture requirement trace to claim 1; illustrated bolt fracture and post-break holding/load relief trace to detailed-description chunks 9ae440fb872f37136a499a50da5672fd and 84de2d5fff965ca14dc473593f2b1b92. The new pivot coupling is traceable to claim 1 and description.

interfaces.rationale: Revision 6 resolves the prior disconnected VANE–LEVER relation with compatible rotational ports and a single interface. The two link couplings use compatible ports/flow and each connection is represented once. External drive is not fabricated.

textbook_application.rationale: Textbook guidance on system boundary and interfaces is used as modeling method to avoid assuming an undisclosed external drive, not as evidence for invention facts.

summary: Revision 6 resolves the prior VANE–LEVER interface gap. The new pivot coupling is supported by the patent’s lever-at-vane-pivot and vane-turning disclosure, and its mechanical_rotational flow is appropriately distinct from the link_motion mechanical_linear flow. The overall SJS is grounded, functionally coherent, claim-traceable, and avoids inventing an external actuator or control system. No actionable unresolved issues found.
